task.question: Prove a period-independent saturated-hole energy modulus and its finite-block mixed-model bridge.
task.domain: Finite Hermitian Toeplitz matrices and supplied periodic paired-exponential cell models.
assumptions: Hole model: marks 0/2 and finite depths; no common phase or uniform depth cap.
Mixed model: mean mass one, marks 0/1/2, one orbit per supplied cell, fixed finite depth cap A.

backend_decision.selection_reason: Portable exact integer/Fraction checks and finite NumPy linear algebra; Python/library imports live-checked.
backend_decision.inventory_boundary: Direct readiness scan only; bundled inventory runner not executed. No assertion about unavailable external MCP services.

precision.mode: exact integer coefficients and Fraction inequalities; binary64 matrices/kernels; 70-digit scalar modulus coefficient
precision.tolerance: 2e-8 times the stated scale in code; tiny negative slacks retained

execution.development: An initial separate 300-hole-model prototype was followed by a six-sample development run of the packaged checker. One final full 120-sample run followed.

exact_subchecks: 153272 finite integer coefficient identities for Q<=96.
8 Fraction certificate comparisons; analytic majorants are separately proved in the note.
limitations: All analytic statements remain proof candidates; no independent receipt or formal proof.
The standalone hole theorem has no uniform depth cap; the mixed theorem retains a fixed finite cap and supplied unit-cell representation.
No actual-zeta representation, multiplicity reduction, depth-tail bound, source profile/localization or arithmetic moment transfer.
Small random mixed-model checks are vacuous under the conservative assembled bound; the finite tolerance rests on the analytic majorants and rational comparisons.
No full-repository local tests, bundled inventory/record runner or upstream Lean build.
The 2^24 partition scale is a scalar parameter, not a simulated matrix dimension.
